scope: Pinned source, caller tracing, upstream test inspection and isolated exact-function probes. No product implementation changes.
bottomLine: Multi-harness subscription-backed workers are baseline parity. Deterministic quota-aware cross-harness handoff with task evidence, ownership fencing, explicit spend policy and supervisor rescue was not established in the inspected Omnigent snapshot.

findings.behavior: Use an existing Claude/Codex subscription login
findings.verdict: Implemented configuration and native-CLI integration; account billing not live-qualified in this pass
findings.limit: A subscription is CLI-bound. Setup permits one configured subscription per CLI, not an account-rotation pool.

findings.behavior: Choose among multiple harnesses and models
findings.verdict: Implemented launch/spawn selection and same-harness turn routing
findings.limit: Task/model compatibility selection is not a response to exhausted subscription quota. A turn router does not switch harness.

findings.behavior: Fallback when the routing service fails
findings.verdict: Implemented and isolated function probe passed
findings.limit: External routing service -> local routing judge. Neither leg transfers worker execution or a subscription.

findings.verdict: Bounded retry of the supplied call is implemented
findings.limit: execute_with_retry invokes the same call_fn; no alternate worker/account selector is supplied there.

findings.behavior: Handle a native worker rate/usage failure
findings.verdict: Implemented reporting, classification and user retry affordances
findings.limit: Some explicit exhausted-credit 429 messages classify as rate_limit_exceeded. Auth and selected gateway-budget errors are distinguished, but this is not a normalized subscription allowance/reset policy.

Fork copies conversation items; native transcript reconstruction is qualified by provider family. No quota-triggered caller found in inspected error paths. A fork does not transfer terminal ownership or prove pending effects safe.

findings.behavior: Recover after a worker result or runner disruption
findings.verdict: Durable child result redelivery and parent wake are implemented
findings.limit: Recovery of result delivery and runner bindings is not automatic subscription failover. A supervisor may replan using tools; that is model-led recovery rather than a deterministic quota controller.

findings.verdict: Cost policy provides approval thresholds and expensive-model downgrade gating
findings.limit: Its max_cost_usd gate can allow work again on a cheaper model; it is not an absolute task spend ceiling or subscription quota balance.

findings.behavior: Automatic subscription exhaustion -> alternate harness -> safe task continuation
findings.verdict: No explicit end-to-end implementation found in bounded inspected production call paths
findings.limit: Not proof of global absence or impossibility through custom agents/extensions. No full app, upstream pytest suite or live subscription test was run.

singleSubscription.needle: # A harness has at most ONE subscription.

limitations: No absence or automatic failover claim is established by probes alone; call-path inspection is separate.
isolatedProbes.context: Classifier cases start from native_turn_error intentionally; native forwarding performs an earlier auth-specific classification. These cases do not claim all 401s stay generic in the full app.

cautions: Existing comments mention a missing _client_executor module and a missing RETRY_ACROSS_HARNESSES design file; those comments were not accepted as proof of a current retry implementation.
The account/rateLimits/updated event appears in a native progress bookkeeping exclusion; this is not evidence of quota scheduling.
Generic OAuth in Overkill is not an official native harness subscription worker adapter.
No comparative task-quality or savings claim is established.

import ast, asyncio, dataclasses, json, logging, re, sys, types
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('research/harnesses/omnigent/source')
def extract(relative,names,ns):
 tree=ast.parse((root/relative).read_text())
 chosen=[]
 for node in tree.body:
  name=getattr(node,'name',None)
  if isinstance(node,ast.Assign): name=next((t.id for t in node.targets if isinstance(t,ast.Name)),None)
  if name in names: chosen.append(node)
 assert len(chosen)==len(names),(relative,set(names)-{getattr(n,'name',None) for n in chosen})
 module=ast.Module(body=[ast.ImportFrom(module='__future__',names=[ast.alias(name='annotations')],level=0),*chosen],type_ignores=[])
 exec(compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(module),str(root/relative),'exec'),ns)
m=types.ModuleType('omnigent_exact_probe');sys.modules[m.__name__]=m
ns=m.__dict__;ns.update({'re':re,'dataclass':dataclasses.dataclass,'_logger':logging.getLogger('probe')})
extract('omnigent/llms/errors.py',{'_CONTENT_LENGTH_PHRASE','_REQUEST_LIMIT_PAIR','_APPROX_BYTES_PER_TOKEN','RequestSizeOverflow','detect_request_size_overflow'},ns)
extract('omnigent/runner/launch_failure.py',{'CODEX_COMPACTION_MODEL_FAILED','_RATE_LIMIT_ERROR','_NATIVE_ERROR_HTTP_STATUS','_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_FRAGMENTS','_TRANSIENT_UPSTREAM_FRAGMENTS','_TRANSIENT_UPSTREAM_STATUSES','_UPSTREAM_CANCELLED_ENVELOPE','_CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED','classify_native_turn_error'},ns)
cases=[('API Error: 429','rate_limit_exceeded'),('API Error: 429 {"error":{"code":"insufficient_quota"}}','rate_limit_exceeded'),('HTTP 429: billing_hard_limit_reached','rate_limit_exceeded'),('HTTP 403: budget has reached its limit','budget_exhausted'),('HTTP 401: unauthorized','native_turn_error'),('API Error: 503 overloaded','transient_upstream_error'),("You've hit your usage limit. Try again tomorrow.",'native_turn_error')]
results=[]
for message,expected in cases:
 actual=ns['classify_native_turn_error']('native_turn_error',message)
 assert actual==expected,(message,actual)
 results.append({'input':message,'classification':actual})
extract('omnigent/server/routing_backend.py',{'RoutingBackends','usable_external','RouterChoice','select_router','RoutedCall','route_with_fallback'},ns)
class Client:
 def __init__(self,fail=False):self.fail=fail;self.calls=[]
 async def route(self,message,models):
  self.calls.append({'message':message,'models':models})
  if self.fail:raise RuntimeError('routing service down')
  return {'harness':'codex','model':'fixture-model'}
async def probe():
 external,local=Client(True),Client()
 result=await ns['route_with_fallback'](ns['RoutingBackends'](external,local),'task',{'codex':['fixture-model']},gateway_backed=True)
 assert result.source=='oss-llm' and len(external.calls)==len(local.calls)==1
 return {'source':result.source,'externalRouterCalls':len(external.calls),'localJudgeCalls':len(local.calls),'workerInvocations':0,'meaning':'Router service fallback; does not execute or transfer a worker task.'}
receipt={'commit':'caa0441fddfcfe407e38be04b55850a128be2dd2','method':'stdlib AST extraction of exact inspected functions and required constants; no competitor app, dependencies, account or vendor request','classifierCases':results,'routerProbe':asyncio.run(probe()),'limitations':['Not the upstream pytest suite.','Not live subscription acceptance.','No absence or automatic failover claim is established by probes alone; call-path inspection is separate.']}
Path('.cache/omnigent-review/probe-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2))
